column1: # Real AppArmor decisions and records, captured from a live kernel enforcing
# profile, arg1, arg2, file owner uid, expected outcome, pid, comm, record the
# kernel logged (- for silence). Kinds: open (arg1 path, arg2 r|w),
# openappend (O_APPEND write), mmap (PROT_EXEC), link (arg1 new link, arg2
# target), exec (arg1 path; outcome is the landing profile, "unconfined", or
# EACCES), chprof (arg1 target profile). Outcome KILL means the process was
# What these rows pin down: a deny rule refuses silently; an audit rule logs
# the ALLOWED access; owner rules deny non-owners loudly; "a" does not satisfy
# a "w" request; mmap(PROT_EXEC) is operation "file_mmap" asking "m"; a link
# names the new path and reports the target last; exec is operation "exec"
# asking "x" alone, so bare "ix" works without "r"; ix inherits, px enters the
# named profile, ux leaves confinement SILENTLY; an immediate change_profile
# denial names the target profile in name= and carries no masks or uids;
# complain mode allows and logs ALLOWED with the would-be denied mask; kill
# mode logs KILLED and SIGKILLs. Probes DAC would refuse never reach AppArmor
# and do not belong here. The two gvisor-root rows settle a production
# question: no wildcard matches "/" itself ("/**" needs a character after the
# slash), so opening the root directory is denied, loudly, unless the profile
# grants "/ r" explicitly; a real kernel and this engine agree. The
# gvisor-file rows pin the converse: bare "file" expands to /{**,}, which DOES
# match "/", so a deny-list profile built on it opens the root directory
# without a record. The engine once expanded it to /** alone, which cannot
# match "/", and every such profile denied ls of the container root. The
# attachtest rows pin attachment: its specification is one AARE expression
# whose alternation attaches /tmp/at/a/bintest and /tmp/at/b/bintest on exec
# Regenerate: load both profiles with apparmor_parser -r, create the fixtures
# (owner-rule files chmod 666, cat copies for exec targets), probe under
